chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ الْمَحْمُودِيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Ali al-Mahmudi, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كَتَبَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِلَيَّ بَعْدَ وَفَاةِ أَبِي: قَدْ مَضَى أَبُوكَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ وَعَنْكَ، وَهُوَ عِنْدَنَا عَلَى حَالٍ مَحْمُودَةٍ وَلَمْ يَتَعَدَّ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْحَالِ

translations.en: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to me after the death of my father: Your father has passed away – may Allah be pleased with him and with you – and he is with us in a praiseworthy state, and he has not exceeded that state.

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the spiritual continuity of the faithful, affirming that the father of the narrator, Ibn Mas'ud, maintained his praiseworthy spiritual state (*hal mahmudah*) after death. It underscores the Shia belief in the enduring status of the righteous within the Imamate’s spiritual oversight, serving as a testament to their unwavering fidelity until the end. The letter acts as a posthumous validation of his piety, reinforcing the concept that death does not sever the bond of spiritual excellence recognized by the Imams.
en.seo_question: What was the spiritual status of the father of Ibn Mas'ud after his death according to Imam al-Jawad?
